Pravendra Singh And 6 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on
9 August, 2024
Author: Raj Beer Singh

Bench: Raj Beer Singh
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:129064
Court No. - 76
Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 23999 of 2024
Applicant :- Pravendra Singh And 6 Others

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- G.A.,Vishnu Murti Tripathi
Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.
1.
Supplementary affidavit filed by learned counsel for the applicants is taken on record.
2. Heard learned counsel for the applicants and learned AGA for the State.

3. This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been preferred for quashing of the entire proceedings, including charge-sheet dated 09.07.2019 as well as cognizance/summoning order dated 16.12.2019, of Case No.140 of 2020, arising out of Case Crime No.95 of 2018, under Sections 498A, 323, 494 I.P.C., Police Station- Mahila Thana, District- Bareilly, pending before the Court of Judicial Magistrate, Bareilly.

sentences.text: It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicants that applicants are innocent and no prima-facie case is made out against them.
It was submitted that impugned summoning order has been passed on a proforma by merely filling in the details of case like sections, police station, next date etc.
Even names of accused persons have not been mentioned in the said impugned summoning order.
It was submitted that the impugned cognizance/summoning order has been passed in a mechanical manner without application of judicial mind.

5. Learned AGA submits that a prima-facie case is made out against the applicants but it could not be disputed that impugned summoning order has been passed on a printed proforma by filling details of the case.
6. I have considered the rival submissions and perused the record.

7. Perusal of record shows that the impugned cognizance and summoning order dated 16.12.2019 has been passed on a printed proforma and merely details of case like name of accused, Sections,
Police Station, Crime Number and Next Date of Listing were filled in the said proforma.
Even names of all the accused persons have not been mentioned in the impugned summoning order.
It is well settled that summoning order has to be passed after considering relevant material and applying judicial mind.

In the instant case, it is apparent that the impugned order has been passed in a mechanical way without applying judicial mind.
8.

It may be stated that there are hundreds of decisions of this Court to the effect that the summoning order cannot be passed on a printed proforma by merely filling in the details of the case,
rather the summoning order must be passed by applying judicial mind.

To mention a few cases,
reference may be made to the case of Ankit Vs. State of U.P., J.I.C. 2010 (1) 432, Basasudin and others Vs. State of U.P., 2011 (1) JIC 335 All, Abdul Rashid and others Vs. State of U.P., 2010 (3) JIC 7661 All, Surender Kumar & others Vs. State of U.P., 2021 (7) ADJ 61, Virendra Kumar Bajpai Vs.
State of U.P. (Application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. No.7972/2022) and Ram Kewal Vs. State of U.P.,
2024:AHC-LKO:5736.
9.

sentences.text: It is a matter of concern that despite repeated directions of this Court, the summoning orders are being passed by some courts on printed proformas.
Summoning of a person as accused is a serious matter and thus, it must reflect the application of judicial mind.

The practice of passing summoning orders on printed proforma by merely filling the details of the case must be stopped forthwith.
10.

In view of the aforesaid, the impugned summoning order dated 16.12.2019, passed by Judicial Magistrate, Bareilly, is hereby set aside and the matter is remitted back to the court concerned to pass the order on cognizance and summoning afresh expeditiously in accordance with law.
11. The instant application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. is finally disposed of in above terms.
